learn.title: Boxes with names
learn.body: A variable is a named place in memory that holds a value. You choose the name, and the computer remembers the value for you. Variables let a program store a score, an age or a result and use it later.

learn.title: Every variable has a type
learn.body: In C you must say what kind of value a variable holds. `int` holds whole numbers like 7, 0 or -12. You declare a variable by writing the type, then the name, then an optional starting value, then a semicolon.

learn.title: Declare and change
learn.body: `%d` prints an int. We cover format codes fully in a later lesson.

learn.title: Assignment is not equality
learn.body: The single `=` means store the value on the right into the variable on the left. So `age = age + 1;` is not a puzzle. It reads the current value, adds 1, and stores the result back.

learn.title: Copying a value
learn.body: Follow this code: `int a = 4;` then `int b = a;` then `a = 10;`.
steps: `b = a` copies the 4 into `b`, so `b` holds 4

learn.title: Choosing names
learn.body: A name may use letters, digits and underscores, but cannot start with a digit. C is case sensitive, so `Total` and `total` are different. Pick names that say what the value means, like `score` instead of `s`.
Give a variable a starting value. An int you never set holds an unpredictable leftover value.

questions.explanation: It declares an `int` called `count` and gives it the starting value 3.

questions.prompt: `int x = 5;` then `x = x + 2;`. What does `x` hold now?
questions.explanation: The right side reads 5, adds 2 and stores 7 back into `x`.

questions.prompt: `int a = 4; int b = a; a = 10;` What does `b` hold? Type the number.
questions.explanation: `b` got a copy of 4. Changing `a` later does not change `b`.

questions.prompt: In C a variable name cannot start with a \_\_.
questions.explanation: Names may contain digits but cannot begin with one.

questions.prompt: Which is a valid variable name?
questions.explanation: Letters, digits and underscores are allowed, no spaces or dashes, and no leading digit.
Capital and lowercase letters make different names.

questions.prompt: Match each line to what it does.
questions.explanation: Declaring creates the variable. Assigning gives it a value. You can do both at once.

questions.prompt: Put these in order to print 21.
questions.explanation: Declare first, then change, then print the current value.
